mechanism_narrative: The sharp acceleration in PARKS mobility (from -50.3 to -20.6 over three weeks) reflects a broad willingness to leave home for outdoor leisure, which typically precedes a parallel rise in retail and recreation visits as people extend outings into shopping and dining trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite PARKS continuing its upward trajectory for at least three more weeks, indicating decoupling of outdoor and retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility crosses above -25 points (continuing its steady weekly recovery from -31.7 to -25.3), this signals a de facto relaxation of state-of-emergency work-from-home guidance, which would restore weekday commuting-linked retail traffic and push RETAIL_REC higher within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -31.7 to -25.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES crosses the -25 threshold but RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the following two weeks, indicating the threshold is not a valid policy-easing signal.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility (both improving roughly 6 points over four weeks) indicates restored multi-stop commuting chains, where transit-enabled trips increasingly combine work and retail stops, amplifying RETAIL_REC growth beyond what either series alone would predict.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over four weeks is no greater than what a model using TRANSIT or WORKPLACES alone would predict, implying no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: The steady decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility (13.9 to 11.4 over four weeks) shows households spending less time confined at home, a behavioral shift toward resuming discretionary outings, which should translate into higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as restrictions are perceived as easing.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL continues to fall while RETAIL_REC fails to increase or decreases over the next two weeks, breaking the inverse relationship.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-February in Tokyo marks the onset of early spring weather and plum blossom season, which seasonally boosts outdoor park visits; this seasonal PARKS uptick spills over into nearby retail and recreation venues as people combine seasonal outings with shopping, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is mid-February, early spring onset in Tokyo
regime_hint: late winter to early spring seasonal transition
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise even though PARKS mobility continues its seasonal increase through the next four weeks, indicating no seasonal spillover.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent narrowing of the GROCERY_PHARM deficit (-12.0 to -5.7) suggests behavioral normalization of errand-running habits; as this proxy nears baseline, it signals reduced caution that should also lift discretionary RETAIL_REC visits within the next week.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM continues its approach to baseline but RETAIL_REC shows no increase within the next week, indicating the two series are not behaviorally linked.

mechanism_narrative: If week-on-week TRANSIT improvement falls below 1 point (a stall after three consecutive weeks of larger gains), it signals that the mobility recovery is plateauing, likely due to residual caution or policy stasis, which would cause RETAIL_REC to flatten or decline over the following week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change falls below 1 point after prior gains exceeded 1 point
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT weekly gains have been shrinking (1.2, 1.4, 3.6 points over three weeks)
failure_condition: TRANSIT week-on-week change drops below 1 point but RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next week, invalidating the stall signal.

mechanism_narrative: A joint pattern of rising WORKPLACES and falling RESIDENTIAL mobility together indicates a coordinated policy-driven unwinding of stay-at-home guidance; when both shift simultaneously, the combined effect on consumer confidence drives a stronger RETAIL_REC increase than either series would independently suggest, over a two-week horizon.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls concurrently but RETAIL_REC gain over two weeks is no larger than predicted by either series alone, indicating no interaction effect.
